chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain of transmission, saying:

The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said regarding a man who acknowledged at the time of his death and said to so-and-so and so-and-so: one of the two has one thousand dirhams owed by me; then he died in that state.
So he عليه السلام said: Whichever of the two establishes the proof, then the money belongs to him. If neither of them establishes the proof, then the money is between them in two equal halves.

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: he acknowledged or confessed a liability
key_terms.عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: at the time of his death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dying person acknowledges a debt but it is unclear which of two people is owed the money?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a dying man's acknowledgement of a debt when the rightful claimant is uncertain between two people. If one claimant produces evidence, he receives the money; otherwise, the amount is divided equally between them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5557 - Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain of transmission that the Commander of the Faithful (as), peace be upon him, said regarding a man who, on his deathbed, confessed;
"So-and-so and so-and-so each have a claim of one thousand dirhams against me," and then he died in that state.
Imam (as) said: "Whoever among them provides evidence has the right to the money. But if neither of them provides evidence, the money is to be divided equally between them."
